sentences.span: That disconnect is the starting point for the latest Equity Volatility Insights note ... AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: BofA names the stock/bond disconnect "the AI put."

sentences.span: in a market with "a relatively fixed supply of attention", macro risk "is struggling to compete for attention with the growth potential of AI narratives." AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying
BofA: macro faces "a high bar to derail the AI trade" / Goldman: "I view higher rates as a headwind to stocks, NOT as a wrecking ball"
sentences.why: Connective framing sentence; the two named tier-1 desks (BofA, Goldman) genuinely offer different lenses on the bond-market stress in the cited notes, consistent with a 'split' framing.

sentences.span: in the absence of an inflation surge -- or a credit problem, more on this in a minute -- I view higher rates as a headwind to stocks, NOT as a wrecking ball.
sentences.why: Direct match to Pasquariello's stated position and conditions.

sentences.span: when 10-year notes back up 2 standard deviations in one month's time, S&P usually begins to show some strain... that rule of thumb was just triggered.
sentences.why: The 2-stdev-per-month framing is a speed-of-move rule, matching the sentence.

sentences.span: I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here.
sentences.why: Exact three-item checklist attributed to Privorotsky.

sentences.span: The French 10-year OAT yield climbed to around 4.92-4.95%, its highest in roughly two decades, and the spread over Bunds pushed through 140bps, the widest since the euro crisis of 2012
sentences.why: Verbatim match of both figures and the 2012 comparison.

sentences.span: Fair value for the 10y OAT-Bund spread stands at 100-110bp ... We cut our French growth forecasts again, to 0.3% and 0.6% for this year and next
sentences.why: Both the fair-value range and the growth-forecast cut appear verbatim in the same BofA note.

sentences.span: The bigger question is structural: can Europe sustain US-driven higher global rates when growth is running at just ~1%? ... GS
sentences.why: The block is tagged GS in the TME compilation, matching the Goldman attribution.

sentences.span: signs of successful negotiations for the 2027 budget - keeping the deficit as close as possible to the government objective of 5.0% - ... could offer support
sentences.why: Matches the budget/deficit-target route to resolving the French spread stress; Goldman source.

sentences.span: 2026 projected hyperscaler issuance of $250bn ... with most of this year's funding ($230bn) completed. 2027 Hyperscaler forecasts of $420bn ... now expecting $420bn ... (vs. $400bn previously) ... 35% of 2027's hyperscaler CapEx spending will be debt funded
sentences.why: All four figures (2026 $250bn/$230bn, 2027 $420bn from $400bn, 35% debt-funded) match exactly.

sentences.span: it will require a hot September CPI print (due 14 October) to make the meeting interesting
sentences.why: Matches date and the October-meeting-contingent framing (corroborated by 18719's "September CPI report on October 14th will be key" and MS Gapen's "bring October back into play").

sentences.span: we are raising our price target to $820 from $750 that is now based on 25x our FY27 EPS estimate (previously 23x)

Muse has quickly become the #1 app in Productivity, with 4.9 stars among 38k ratings ... generated >3mn app installs in the US during its first 16 days ... ChatGPT ... took ~35 days to match Muse's cumulative downloads in its first 16 days
sentences.why: All figures (rank, rating, ratings count, installs, 16 days, ChatGPT's ~35 days) match exactly.

sentences.span: Meta has been very generous with the usage limits on the free tier ... we do not think there is a large incentive for users to upgrade ... Muse could represent ~Mid-SD% of Meta's 2030 revenue ... roughly $25-$50 per Muse user in CapEx
sentences.why: Matches free-tier/acquisition framing, mid-single-digit 2030 revenue share, and $25-$50 capex-per-user figure.
